issues.legal_issue: A correction power enacted after an administrative notice does not authorize that earlier notice, although it permits correction proceedings to be initiated after the power takes effect.
material_facts: Rents had previously been fixed by a published order.
Officials issued a notice proposing further rent reductions before the amendment creating an express power to correct errors in the earlier order had taken effect.
The property owner sought a writ restraining proceedings under the notice.
issues.conclusion: The later correction power operated prospectively and did not make the earlier notice an exercise of that power. The government remained free to initiate fresh proceedings under the amended law.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3-B, added to the Rent Reduction Act by the amending enactment, authorized the government to correct qualifying errors in an existing order. The Court construed that authority as enabling action after the amendment came into force, not as retrospectively authorizing a notice issued earlier. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.writ_challenge_to_administrative_notice: A property owner sought judicial restraint of administrative proceedings initiated by a notice.
predicates.correction_authority_created_after_notic: The legislature created an express power to correct an earlier administrative order after the challenged notice had been issued.

issues.definition: When a property owner challenges proceedings initiated by a notice and the express correction authority was created only afterward, the earlier notice is not authorized by that later authority.

issues.legal_issue: A notice proposing a change to an earlier determination does not qualify as a notice for correcting an error when it does not identify an error in that determination.
material_facts: Officials issued a notice proposing reductions to rents that had already been fixed.
The notice described the proposed reductions but did not allege that the earlier fixation contained an error.
The government later sought to defend the notice as initiating correction of an error.
issues.conclusion: The notice could not be treated as one issued to initiate proceedings for correction of an error under the later correction power.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3-B permitted correction of an error in an earlier order, and the Court held that the challenged notice did not fit that process because it contained no allegation of error. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.writ_challenge_to_administrative_notice: A property owner sought judicial restraint of administrative proceedings initiated by a notice.
predicates.notice_proposes_change_to_prior_determin: Officials used a notice to propose changing a determination that had already been made.
predicates.notice_does_not_identify_error: The notice proposed a change without stating that the earlier determination contained an error.

issues.definition: A challenged notice proposing a change to an earlier determination is outside an error-correction process when it does not identify an error in that determination.

issues.legal_issue: A provision validating completed orders or notifications that cancel or correct an earlier order does not validate a notice that merely proposes a future change.
material_facts: The challenged document invited objections to proposed rent reductions and initiated an inquiry.
The document did not itself cancel or correct the earlier rent-fixing order.
The amending enactment validated certain pre-existing orders or notifications that cancelled or corrected earlier orders.
issues.conclusion: The validation provision did not validate the challenged notice.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5 of the amending enactment applied to pre-existing orders or notifications cancelling or correcting an earlier order, if they would have been valid under the amended law. The Court held that a notice proposing a future reduction was not within that description. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.writ_challenge_to_administrative_notice: A property owner sought judicial restraint of administrative proceedings initiated by a notice.
predicates.notice_only_invites_objections_to_propos: Officials used the document to invite objections to a change they proposed to make later.
predicates.notice_does_not_itself_cancel_or_correct: The document did not itself cancel or correct the earlier order.

issues.definition: A challenged notice is not validated as a completed correction when it only invites objections to a proposed change and does not itself cancel or correct the earlier order.
